title: Maximum Subarray

understand.question: Given an array of integers (which may include negatives and zero), what is the largest total sum you can get from a non-empty contiguous slice?
understand.plainExplanation: Think of daily profit-and-loss numbers for a shop. You want to pick one unbroken stretch of consecutive days (at least one day long) whose combined profit is as large as possible.
understand.inputMeaning: A non-empty integer array nums (for example [-2, 5, -1, 4, -6, 2]).
understand.outputMeaning: A single integer: the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of length >= 1.
rules: The chosen elements must be contiguous (adjacent in the original array without skipping elements in the middle).
The subarray must be non-empty (at least one element must be selected, even if every number in the array is negative).
You only return the maximum sum value, not the slice indices.

terms.definition: A contiguous slice nums[left..right] with 0 <= left <= right < n. Unlike a subsequence, you cannot skip elements inside the slice.
The largest sum of a subarray that MUST end at the current index i.
The largest subarray sum seen across all ending indices processed so far.

example1.whyValid: The contiguous slice [5, -1, 4] from index 1 through index 3 sums to 5 + (-1) + 4 = 8. Including index 0 (-2) lowers it to 6, and extending to index 4 (-6) drops it to 2.

example2.whyEdgeCase: All numbers are negative! Because the subarray must be non-empty, you cannot return 0 by picking nothing. The least-negative single element [-2] gives the maximum sum -2.

steps.title: Start at index 0 with nums[0]
steps.description: Initialize currentSum = -2 and bestSum = -2 using the first element (never 0, so all-negative inputs work).

steps.title: Index 1 (value 5): restart fresh at 5
steps.description: Extending the previous sum (-2 + 5 = 3) is worse than starting fresh at 5! So currentSum = max(5, 3) = 5, and bestSum updates to 5.

state.caption: Drop negative prefix [-2]; start fresh at index 1.

steps.title: Index 2 (value -1): extend positive prefix
steps.description: Extending gives 5 + (-1) = 4, which beats starting at -1 alone. Keep currentSum = 4; bestSum stays 5.

steps.title: Index 3 (value 4): new peak sum 8!
steps.description: Extending gives 4 + 4 = 8 (beating 4 alone). currentSum = 8 and bestSum improves to 8.

steps.title: Indices 4 & 5 (-6 then +2): finish scan
steps.description: At index 4 (-6), currentSum = max(-6, 8 - 6) = 2. At index 5 (+2), currentSum = max(2, 2 + 2) = 4. Neither beats bestSum = 8, so return 8.

approaches.name: Brute Force Running Sum
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Try every starting index i and accumulate sums forward to j.
approaches.coreIdea: Fix every starting index i, maintain a running sum as ending index j moves right, and track the global maximum.
steps: For each start index i from 0 to n - 1, reset running = 0.
For each end index j from i to n - 1, add nums[j] to running and update bestSum = max(bestSum, running).
approaches.whyItWorks: Every non-empty subarray is uniquely identified by its pair (i, j) with 0 <= i <= j < n, so checking all of them guarantees finding the maximum.
approaches.whenToUse: Good baseline to verify small inputs against faster algorithms.
approaches.diagramNote: Fixes start i=1 and extends j rightward while summing 5 -> 4 -> 8 -> 2 -> 4.

diagram.caption: Best running sum from i=1 occurs at j=3 (sum = 8).

approaches.name: Prefix Sum + Minimum Prefix Tracking
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Maximize prefixSum[j] - min(prefixSum[i]) for i < j.
approaches.coreIdea: Any subarray sum nums[i..j] equals prefixSum - previousPrefixSum. Tracking the smallest prefix sum seen before the current position lets us compute the best subarray ending here in O(1).
steps: Initialize prefix = 0, minPrefix = 0, and best = nums[0].
For each value x in nums, add x to prefix.
approaches.whyItWorks: Subtracting the lowest earlier prefix sum maximizes prefix - earlierPrefix, while updating minPrefix AFTER evaluating best ensures the chosen subarray is non-empty.
approaches.whenToUse: Great when bridging prefix-sum problems (like Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock or Subarray Sum variations).
approaches.diagramNote: Tracks cumulative prefix sums: subtracting minPrefix (-2 at idx 0) from prefix (6 at idx 3) gives 6 - (-2) = 8.

diagram.caption: Array shows prefix sums at each index.

approaches.name: Divide and Conquer
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Split at mid and take max(leftBest, rightBest, bestCrossingMid).
approaches.coreIdea: Recursively split the array into left and right halves. The best subarray lies entirely in the left half, entirely in the right half, or crosses the midpoint.
steps: Base case: if left == right, return nums[left].
Recursively compute leftBest on [left..mid] and rightBest on [mid+1..right].
Scan left from mid down to left to find maxLeftSuffix; scan right from mid+1 up to right to find maxRightPrefix.
approaches.whyItWorks: Every subarray in [left..right] either skips the boundary between mid and mid+1 or spans across it, and the best crossing slice must combine the best suffix ending at mid with the best prefix starting at mid+1.
approaches.whenToUse: Required if a follow-up asks for a divide-and-conquer solution or when extending to Segment Tree range-max-subarray queries.

complexity.variables: n = length of nums (recursion stack depth is log2 n)

approaches.diagramNote: Splits at mid=2: best left [5,-1] = 5, best right [4] = 4, and best crossing [5,-1] + [4] = 8.

diagram.caption: Crossing sum 8 beats leftBest (5) and rightBest (4).

approaches.name: Tabulated Dynamic Programming (dp[i])
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Store dp[i] = best subarray sum ending exactly at index i.
approaches.coreIdea: Define dp[i] as the maximum subarray sum that ends at index i. Each entry depends solely on dp[i - 1] and nums[i].
steps: Allocate dp of size n with dp[0] = nums[0] and best = dp[0].
For i from 1 to n - 1, compute dp[i] = max(nums[i], dp[i - 1] + nums[i]).
Update best = max(best, dp[i]) and return best.
approaches.whyItWorks: Any subarray ending at i either contains only nums[i] or appends nums[i] to a subarray ending at i - 1. Taking max(nums[i], dp[i - 1] + nums[i]) captures the optimal choice.
approaches.whenToUse: Helpful when learning the DP recurrence before compressing dp[] into a single variable.
approaches.diagramNote: Stores dp[i] = max subarray sum ending at index i. Maximum value in dp[] is 8 at index 3.

diagram.caption: Array shows tabulated dp[i] values; global max is 8.

approaches.name: Kadane's Algorithm (Space-Optimized DP)
approaches.recommendedTradeOff: Achieves the optimal O(n) worst-case time in one pass while compressing the DP table down to O(1) auxiliary space with zero allocations.
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Carry the running subarray sum only while it helps; otherwise restart at nums[i].
approaches.coreIdea: Keep only two numbers: currentSum (best subarray ending at the current index) and bestSum (best seen anywhere). If currentSum + nums[i] < nums[i], discard the earlier negative prefix and restart at nums[i].
steps: Initialize currentSum = nums[0] and bestSum = nums[0].
For i from 1 to n - 1, set currentSum = max(nums[i], currentSum + nums[i]).
approaches.whyItWorks: Since dp[i] only reads dp[i - 1], storing dp[i - 1] in currentSum preserves the exact same DP recurrence while discarding older prefixes whenever they become negative.
approaches.whenToUse: Default optimal solution for maximum contiguous subarray sum.

code.Ruby:
def max_sub_array(nums)
  current = best = nums[0]
  nums[1..].each do |x|
    current = [x, current + x].max
    best = [best, current].max
  end
  best
end
code.Erlang:
-spec max_sub_array(Nums :: [integer()]) -> integer().
max_sub_array([H | T]) ->
  max_sub_array(T, H, H).

max_sub_array([], _Cur, Best) -> Best;
max_sub_array([H | T], Cur, Best) ->
  Nxt = max(H, Cur + H),
  max_sub_array(T, Nxt, max(Best, Nxt)).
code.Racket:
(define/contract (max-sub-array nums)
  (-> (listof exact-integer?) exact-integer?)
  (let loop ([rest (cdr nums)] [cur (car nums)] [best (car nums)])
    (if (null? rest)
        best
        (let* ([x (car rest)]
               [nxt (max x (+ cur x))])
          (loop (cdr rest) nxt (max best nxt))))))
